title: Implement Saga Pattern for Distributed Transactions
question: Design a distributed transaction system for an e-commerce order processing workflow using Saga pattern. Requirements: 1) Order placement involves multiple services: OrderService creates order, PaymentService charges customer, InventoryService reserves items, ShippingService schedules delivery, 2) Each service has its own database (no 2PC/XA), 3) Implement compensating transactions for each step to handle failures (refund payment, release inventory, cancel shipping if any step fails), 4) Maintain data consistency across services despite failures, 5) Support both orchestration-based saga (central coordinator) and choreography-based saga (event-driven), 6) Handle idempotency (prevent duplicate operations if messages are reprocessed). Discuss: implementing orchestration saga with OrderOrchestrator service that calls each service sequentially and tracks state, storing saga state in database with current_step and status, implementing compensating transactions (@Transactional methods to undo: cancelPayment(), releaseInventory(), cancelShipping()), using Kafka/RabbitMQ for choreography where each service publishes events (OrderCreated → PaymentService → PaymentCompleted → InventoryService), implementing Outbox pattern to ensure reliable event publishing (atomically save event to outbox table with business transaction, background poller publishes events), handling partial failures and retries with idempotency keys, implementing timeout-based compensation (if payment doesn't complete in 30s, start rollback), saga state visualization for debugging, and trade-offs between orchestration (centralized, easier to understand) vs choreography (decentralized, more scalable).

title: Migrate Monolith to Microservices Using Strangler Fig Pattern
question: Design a migration strategy to incrementally move a legacy monolithic application to microservices without big bang rewrite. Requirements: 1) Monolith is a large Java application with 500K+ LOC, single database, tightly coupled modules, 2) Business requires continuous operation during migration (no downtime), 3) Migrate high-priority modules first (user authentication, payment processing), 4) Support gradual traffic shifting from monolith to new microservices, 5) Handle data synchronization between monolith database and new service databases during transition, 6) Minimize risk and allow rollback if issues arise. Discuss: implementing API Gateway as routing layer to intercept all requests, routing new feature requests to microservices while legacy requests go to monolith, using feature flags for gradual traffic shifting (route 10% → 50% → 100% to new service), extracting bounded contexts from monolith (start with least coupled modules), implementing Anti-Corruption Layer to translate between monolith and microservice data models, handling dual-write problem during migration (write to both monolith DB and new service DB, eventually remove monolith writes), using Change Data Capture (CDC) with Debezium to sync data from monolith to microservices, implementing compensation logic if microservice call fails (fallback to monolith), monitoring with distributed tracing to compare monolith vs microservice performance, and decomposition strategies (start with stateless services, then stateful, avoid breaking foreign key relationships too early).

title: Implement CQRS and Event Sourcing for Audit and Scalability
question: Design a system using CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation) and Event Sourcing for a banking application. Requirements: 1) Separate read and write models for scalability (heavy read traffic, moderate writes), 2) Store all state changes as immutable events (audit trail requirement), 3) Reconstruct current account state by replaying events, 4) Support different read models optimized for different queries (account balance, transaction history, monthly reports), 5) Handle eventual consistency between write and read models, 6) Support temporal queries (what was the balance on Jan 15th?). Discuss: implementing command side with AccountCommandService handling commands (CreateAccount, DepositMoney, WithdrawMoney) that generate events, storing events in event_store table with aggregate_id, event_type, event_data (JSON), version, timestamp, implementing optimistic locking with version column to prevent concurrent modifications, publishing events to Kafka after persistence, implementing projection services that consume events and build read models (account_balance table, transaction_history table, monthly_summary materialized view), handling eventual consistency in UI (show "processing" state until read model catches up), implementing event replay for rebuilding read models (consume all events from beginning), snapshotting for performance (store account state snapshot every 100 events, replay only recent events), handling schema evolution (versioned events, upcasting old events to new schema), implementing temporal queries by replaying events up to specific timestamp, and trade-offs (complexity vs auditability and scalability).

title: API Gateway with Backend for Frontend (BFF) Pattern
question: Design an API Gateway that aggregates data from multiple microservices for different client types (web, mobile, IoT). Requirements: 1) Web app needs detailed data (full user profile, all order details), mobile app needs minimal data (summary only) due to bandwidth constraints, IoT devices need only specific metrics, 2) Implement Backend for Frontend (BFF) pattern with different gateway logic per client type, 3) Aggregate data from UserService, OrderService, ProductService in single API call to reduce round trips, 4) Handle partial failures gracefully (if ProductService fails, still return user and order data), 5) Implement caching to reduce backend load, 6) Support API versioning for backward compatibility. Discuss: creating separate BFF gateways (WebBFF, MobileBFF, IoTBFF) with client-specific logic, implementing aggregation endpoint that makes parallel calls to multiple services using CompletableFuture, handling circuit breaker at gateway level to fail fast when services are down, implementing fallback responses for partial failures (return cached product data if ProductService is unavailable), using Redis for response caching with TTL, implementing API versioning with /v1/ and /v2/ prefixes in gateway routes, request/response transformation at gateway (filter sensitive fields, map DTOs), implementing rate limiting per client tier, GraphQL alternative for flexible client queries, and trade-offs between BFF complexity vs client optimization.

title: Handle Eventual Consistency in Distributed System
question: Design strategies to handle eventual consistency in a social media application. Requirements: 1) User posts content, followers see post in their timeline (fan-out), 2) Post likes counter should be eventually consistent (don't need exact count immediately), 3) User can edit/delete post, updates propagate to all followers' timelines, 4) Handle race conditions (user likes, then post is deleted), 5) Support compensating updates (if post processing fails, rollback timeline entries), 6) Provide user feedback about consistency lag ("updating..."). Discuss: using event-driven architecture with PostCreated, PostUpdated, PostDeleted events published to Kafka, TimelineService consumes events and updates user timelines asynchronously, implementing eventual consistency with versioned events (each event has version/timestamp), handling out-of-order events by checking event version, implementing optimistic UI updates (show like immediately in UI, send async request to backend, revert if fails), using CRDT (Conflict-free Replicated Data Type) for like counters that can be incremented concurrently, implementing read-your-own-writes consistency (user sees their own posts immediately even if not propagated), showing staleness indicators in UI ("data may be up to 5 seconds old"), implementing compensating updates via tombstone events (PostDeleted event removes from timelines), handling dual-write problem (write to PostService database and publish event atomically using Outbox pattern), and monitoring consistency lag with metrics.

title: Data Consistency Patterns Across Microservices
question: Implement different data consistency patterns for various business requirements. Requirements: 1) Strong consistency for payment transactions (can't lose money), 2) Eventual consistency for user profile updates (acceptable delay), 3) Causal consistency for chat messages (replies must appear after original message), 4) Implement data replication across services while maintaining consistency, 5) Handle network partitions and split-brain scenarios, 6) Support cross-service queries without joining databases. Discuss: using distributed transactions with Saga pattern for payment (strong consistency requirement), implementing 2PC/XA only when absolutely necessary (understand CAP theorem trade-offs), using event sourcing for user profiles with eventual consistency (ProfileUpdated events), implementing causal consistency in chat with vector clocks or Lamport timestamps, creating read-only replicas of data in consuming services (UserService publishes UserUpdated events, OrderService maintains user cache), implementing database views or materialized views for cross-service queries, using API composition pattern (gateway aggregates data from multiple services), implementing CQRS with separate read/write models, handling network partitions with conflict resolution strategies (last-write-wins, version vectors, application-specific merge), implementing anti-entropy mechanisms for eventual consistency (background reconciliation jobs), and monitoring data consistency with health checks and metrics.

title: Implement Service Mesh for Service-to-Service Communication
question: Design service-to-service communication infrastructure using service mesh (Istio/Linkerd). Requirements: 1) Implement mTLS for all inter-service communication, 2) Distributed tracing across all services, 3) Traffic management (canary deployments, A/B testing, traffic shifting), 4) Automatic retries and circuit breaking, 5) Service-level metrics and observability, 6) Zero-trust security model. Discuss: deploying Istio with control plane (istiod) and data plane (Envoy sidecar proxies injected into each pod), implementing automatic mTLS with Istio's built-in CA for certificate management, configuring PeerAuthentication to enforce mTLS across namespace, integrating with Jaeger for distributed tracing (Envoy sidecars automatically inject trace headers), implementing VirtualServices for traffic routing (50% to v1, 50% to v2 for canary deployment), using DestinationRules for circuit breaker configuration (consecutive errors threshold, connection pool settings), implementing retry policies with exponential backoff, collecting service metrics with Prometheus (request rate, error rate, latency), visualizing service topology with Kiali, implementing authorization policies for zero-trust (only OrderService can call PaymentService), configuring egress gateways for external service calls, handling service mesh overhead (added latency from sidecar, resource consumption), and gradual migration strategy (start with non-critical services, expand to all).

title: Multi-Tenancy Architecture in Microservices
question: Design multi-tenant architecture where each customer's data is isolated. Requirements: 1) Support 1000+ tenants with varying data sizes (small tenants: 100MB, large: 100GB), 2) Each tenant must have complete data isolation (compliance requirement), 3) Different service tiers (basic, premium) with different resource limits, 4) Route requests to correct tenant context automatically, 5) Support tenant-specific customizations (branding, workflows), 6) Efficient resource utilization (shared infrastructure). Discuss: propagating tenant context through all service calls via JWT claims or custom header (X-Tenant-ID), implementing TenantContext with ThreadLocal for accessing tenant_id in business logic, using @Aspect to automatically inject tenant_id into all queries (e.g., SELECT * FROM orders WHERE tenant_id = ?), implementing database isolation strategies (separate schema per tenant in shared database, or separate database per large tenant), using Hibernate filters to automatically add tenant_id to all queries, implementing multi-tenant caching with tenant-aware cache keys (tenant_id:user_id), routing to tenant-specific service instances for large tenants (dedicated pods with label tenant=acme-corp), implementing tenant onboarding workflow (create schema, seed data, provision resources), handling cross-tenant queries for super-admin (disable tenant filter temporarily), implementing rate limiting per tenant based on tier, storing tenant-specific configuration in tenant_config table, and monitoring per-tenant resource usage for billing.

title: Distributed Caching Strategy Across Microservices
question: Design distributed caching strategy to improve performance and reduce database load. Requirements: 1) Cache frequently accessed data (user profiles, product catalog), 2) Handle cache invalidation when data changes, 3) Implement cache-aside and write-through patterns, 4) Support cache warming for critical data, 5) Handle cache stampede (thundering herd), 6) Maintain consistency between cache and database. Discuss: using Redis cluster as distributed cache shared across microservices, implementing cache-aside pattern (check cache first, load from DB if miss, populate cache), implementing write-through for critical data (write to cache and DB simultaneously), using Spring Cache abstraction with @Cacheable, @CacheEvict, @CachePut annotations, implementing cache invalidation via events (UserUpdated event → UserService evicts cache → other services listen and evict their caches), using pub/sub for cache invalidation broadcast, implementing TTL-based expiration for eventual consistency, handling cache stampede with locking (only first request loads from DB, others wait) or probabilistic early expiration, implementing multi-level caching (local caffeine cache + distributed Redis cache), cache warming at application startup for critical data, implementing circuit breaker pattern for cache failures (fallback to DB if Redis is down), monitoring cache hit ratio and sizing cache appropriately, and handling cache consistency with versioning or ETags.

title: Implement Bulkhead Pattern for Resource Isolation
question: Design resource isolation using bulkhead pattern to prevent cascading failures. Requirements: 1) Application has critical path (order processing) and non-critical path (analytics/reporting), 2) Heavy analytics queries shouldn't impact order processing performance, 3) Isolate thread pools for different operations, 4) Limit resources per tenant to prevent noisy neighbor problem, 5) Implement separate database connection pools, 6) Monitor resource utilization per bulkhead. Discuss: creating separate thread pools using @Async with custom executors (criticalExecutor with 50 threads for orders, analyticsExecutor with 10 threads for reports), implementing Resilience4j bulkhead with maxConcurrentCalls to limit concurrent executions, using separate HikariCP connection pools for critical vs analytical queries (criticalDataSource with min 20 connections, analyticsDataSource with min 5), implementing semaphore-based bulkhead for synchronous operations, creating separate service instances for critical vs non-critical workloads (deploy OrderService with high resources, AnalyticsService with lower resources), implementing per-tenant rate limiting with token bucket algorithm, monitoring thread pool metrics (active threads, queue size, rejected tasks), implementing graceful degradation (reject non-critical requests when system is under load), using Kubernetes resource limits (CPU/memory) to enforce isolation at container level, and handling thread pool exhaustion with proper error responses and circuit breakers.
